I'll use `Essential hypertension` (320128) as the anchor, using `condition_ancestor` to capture the whole hypertension descendant tree for the adult cohort, then rank co-occurring conditions. Let me build the cohort and co-occurrence ranking.

arguments.sql_query:
-- Adults (age >=18 at first HTN dx) with any hypertension diagnosis (descendants of Essential HTN 320128 + Hypertensive disorder 316866)
WITH htn_concepts AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ca.descendant_concept_id AS concept_id
  FROM omop.concept_ancestor ca
  WHERE ca.ancestor_concept_id IN (316866, 320128)  -- Hypertensive disorder, Essential hypertension
),
htn_pts AS (
  SELECT co.person_id, MIN(co.condition_start_date) AS first_htn
  FROM omop.condition_occurrence co
  JOIN htn_concepts h ON co.condition_concept_id = h.concept_id
  GROUP BY co.person_id
),
adult_htn AS (
  SELECT hp.person_id
  FROM htn_pts hp
  JOIN omop.person p ON p.person_id = hp.person_id
  WHERE DATEDIFF(year, DATEFROMPARTS(p.year_of_birth,1,1), hp.first_htn) >= 18
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS adult_htn_patients FROM adult_htn;

WITH htn_concepts AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ca.descendant_concept_id AS concept_id

),
htn_pts AS (
  SELECT co.person_id, MIN(co.condition_start_date) AS first_htn
  FROM omop.condition_occurrence co
  JOIN htn_concepts h ON co.condition_concept_id = h.concept_id
  GROUP BY co.person_id
),
adult_htn AS (
  SELECT hp.person_id
  FROM htn_pts hp
  JOIN omop.person p ON p.person_id = hp.person_id
  WHERE DATEDIFF(year, DATEFROMPARTS(p.year_of_birth,1,1), hp.first_htn) >= 18
),
comorb AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT co.person_id, co.condition_concept_id
  FROM omop.condition_occurrence co
  JOIN adult_htn a ON a.person_id = co.person_id
  WHERE co.condition_concept_id NOT IN (SELECT concept_id FROM htn_concepts)
    AND co.condition_concept_id <> 0
)
SELECT TOP 40 c.concept_id, c.concept_name,
       COUNT(DISTINCT cm.person_id) AS n_patients,
       CAST(100.0*COUNT(DISTINCT cm.person_id)/446516 AS DECIMAL(5,1)) AS pct
FROM comorb cm
JOIN omop.concept c ON c.concept_id = cm.condition_concept_id
GROUP BY c.concept_id, c.concept_name
ORDER BY n_patients DESC;

The raw list mixes true comorbidities with symptoms/findings. Let me get cleaner comorbidity counts by rolling up to major condition categories, and compute a background prevalence to show enrichment (which is what makes co-occurrence meaningful). I'll also pull the frequently co-occurring cardiometabolic cluster together.

arguments.sql_query:
WITH htn_concepts AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ca.descendant_concept_id AS concept_id
  FROM omop.concept_ancestor ca
  WHERE ca.ancestor_concept_id IN (316866, 320128)
),
htn_pts AS (
  SELECT co.person_id, MIN(co.condition_start_date) AS first_htn
  FROM omop.condition_occurrence co
  JOIN htn_concepts h ON co.condition_concept_id = h.concept_id
  GROUP BY co.person_id
),
adult_htn AS (
  SELECT hp.person_id
  FROM htn_pts hp
  JOIN omop.person p ON p.person_id = hp.person_id
  WHERE DATEDIFF(year, DATEFROMPARTS(p.year_of_birth,1,1), hp.first_htn) >= 18
),
grp AS (
  SELECT 'Hyperlipidemia/dyslipidemia' AS comorbidity, 432867 AS anc UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Type 2 diabetes mellitus', 201826 UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Obesity', 433736 UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Chronic kidney disease', 46271022 UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Coronary atherosclerosis / IHD', 317576 UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Atrial fibrillation', 313217 UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Heart failure', 316139 UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Obstructive sleep apnea', 442588 UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Depressive disorder', 440383 UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Hypothyroidism', 140673
)
SELECT g.comorbidity,
       COUNT(DISTINCT co.person_id) AS n_in_htn,
       CAST(100.0*COUNT(DISTINCT co.person_id)/446516 AS DECIMAL(5,1)) AS pct_of_htn
FROM grp g
JOIN omop.concept_ancestor ca ON ca.ancestor_concept_id = g.anc
JOIN omop.condition_occurrence co ON co.condition_concept_id = ca.descendant_concept_id
JOIN adult_htn a ON a.person_id = co.person_id
GROUP BY g.comorbidity
ORDER BY n_in_htn DESC;

## Comorbidities co-occurring with hypertension

Adult hypertension cohort: **446,516 patients** (age ≥18 at first HTN diagnosis), OMOP CDM database. Ranked by patients with ≥1 diagnosis (concept trees rolled up to parent disorders):

| Comorbidity | % of HTN cohort |
|---|---|
| Hyperlipidemia / dyslipidemia | **48.5%** |
| Depressive disorder | 19.1% |
| Type 2 diabetes mellitus | 18.8% |
| Coronary atherosclerosis / ischemic heart disease | 18.6% |
| Chronic kidney disease | 17.2% |
| Obesity | 16.7% |
| Atrial fibrillation | 13.8% |
| Hypothyroidism | 13.3% |
| Heart failure | 13.1% |
| Obstructive sleep apnea | 11.5% |

(Symptom/finding codes like chest pain, dyspnea, anemia and abnormal ECG also ranked high in the raw counts but are not distinct diseases, so I collapsed to true disorders.)

## Shared biological pathways

The top co-occurring conditions are not independent — they cluster into a few mechanistic groups.

**1. Insulin resistance / metabolic syndrome** — links hyperlipidemia, T2DM, obesity, OSA, and HTN itself.
- Hyperinsulinemia drives renal sodium retention and sympathetic activation → raises BP.
- Adipose tissue is endocrine: excess leptin/reduced adiponectin and free fatty acids promote both dyslipidemia and vascular insulin resistance.
- This is the single strongest cluster — obesity → insulin resistance is the common upstream node for four of the ten comorbidities.

**2. RAAS (renin–angiotensin–aldosterone) overactivity** — links HTN, CKD, and heart failure.
- Angiotensin II raises BP, drives glomerular hyperfiltration/fibrosis (CKD), and induces cardiac hypertrophy and remodeling (HF). CKD in turn worsens volume/sodium handling — a bidirectional loop.

**3. Endothelial dysfunction & chronic inflammation / oxidative stress** — links HTN, atherosclerosis (IHD), CKD, and diabetes.
- Reduced nitric-oxide bioavailability plus elevated ROS, NF-κB signaling and inflammatory cytokines accelerate atherosclerotic plaque and microvascular injury shared across all four.

**4. Sympathetic nervous system overactivity** — links OSA, HTN, atrial fibrillation, and heart failure.
- Intermittent nocturnal hypoxia (OSA) and neurohormonal activation raise catecholamine tone, promoting atrial remodeling/AF and pressure load.

**5. Endocrine/metabolic modulation** — hypothyroidism raises diastolic BP and LDL (impaired lipid clearance), and depression is linked via HPA-axis and sympathetic dysregulation plus shared inflammatory signaling.

**Caveats:** These are association counts within a single OMOP EHR dataset (not adjusted for age/sex or compared to a non-HTN control, so figures reflect co-occurrence, not causal enrichment). The pathway links are established literature-level mechanisms, not derived from this dataset.
